transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I've started going out of my way to avoid driving or even being a passenger in cars, and it's completely taking over my life. It has shrunk my world so much, and I realized I just can't seem to move past this on my own.
Did this intense fear and avoidance of cars start after you experienced or witnessed a specific traumatic event, such as a car accident?

Yes, it all started after a really bad car accident about two years and three months ago. A drunk driver crossed the center line and hit my car head-on, trapping me inside until rescuers could cut me out. I later found out that the other driver died at the scene, and I've just been stuck in this fear ever since.
Since the accident, do you experience distressing, unwanted memories of the crash, nightmares, or sudden flashbacks where you feel like it's happening again?

Yes, I do. Out of nowhere, especially if I hear tires screech or see headlights coming toward me, I’ll suddenly feel like I'm right back in that car, pinned and smelling the gasoline. My heart just takes off like it’s happening all over again.
Since the accident, have you also been feeling constantly on edge, easily startled, or having trouble sleeping or concentrating?

Yes, my brain feels foggy a lot of the time, making it really hard to concentrate on simple things like reading a recipe or deciding what to cook. I also feel incredibly on edge, especially in a car, where I'm constantly glued to the mirrors and watching other drivers like they're about to hit us.
Since the accident, have you noticed any persistent changes in your mood, such as feeling detached from loved ones or losing interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Yes, I really have. I used to love my dance classes and planning menus for my pop-up dinners, but now I just feel completely flat and end up going home to watch TV instead. I also feel like there's this invisible wall between me and my family or friends, because they're all moving on with their lives while I'm just stuck in this bubble of fear.
Have these distressing feelings, flashbacks, and sleep difficulties been happening regularly for at least a month since the accident?
Yes, it's been much longer than just a month. These feelings and fears have been hanging over me constantly ever since the crash a little over two years ago, and they just haven't let up at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) following a life-threatening motor vehicle accident 2 years and 3 months ago. The patient experiences recurrent intrusive flashbacks triggered by trauma reminders, persistent avoidance of vehicles, negative alterations in mood and cognition (detachment, anhedonia, emotional flattening), and marked hyperarousal (hypervigilance and concentration difficulties). These symptoms have persisted for over two years and cause significant functional impairment.
